question: Which of the following steps promoted the growth of the economy as a whole by stimulating the development of industrial and tertiary sectors?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Planning**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Planning** was the key factor that promoted overall economic growth by stimulating the **industrial and tertiary sectors**.
 
• After independence, India adopted a **planned economic approach**, mainly through the **Five-Year Plans** initiated in 1951.
 
• These plans focused on systematic development across all sectors, **including agriculture, industry, and services (tertiary sector).**
 
• Planning directly contributed to industrial growth through:
 
 
• **Public Sector Enterprises (PSUs):** Heavy industries like steel, coal, and petroleum were set up under government control.
 
• **Infrastructure Development:** Dams, power plants, and transport networks were developed to support industries.
 
• **Industrial Policies:** The **Industrial Policy of 1956** encouraged the growth of core industries and limited private sector participation.
 
• **Small and Cottage Industries:** Special support was given to small-scale industries to boost employment and production.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The tertiary sector (services sector) also expanded due to planning:
 
 
• **Banking & Finance:** Nationalization of banks (1969) improved credit availability for industries.
 
• **Transport & Communication:** Roads, railways, and telecommunication networks were expanded.
 
• **Education & Healthcare:** Planned investments led to better literacy rates and healthcare, improving the workforce quality.
 
• **Trade & Commerce:** Economic planning led to urbanization, increasing demand for retail, tourism, and IT services.
